reasons: The rule is a 'missing' kind and the cited General Matters section (paragraphs (a)-(i), ending with a headings clause) contains no insurance covenant; the rationale states a full-text search for 'insurance' returns nothing, which is consistent with the excerpts provided.

Insertion is well-placed as a new Section 20(j) in the miscellaneous section and tracks the playbook's model language closely (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where Customer Data is processed, workers' compensation, certificates on request), with party names correctly localized to Garman/Sparkling.

Applicability is justified: the vendor installs software at Authorized Locations and performs data conversion, so it both attends our premises and processes our data — the walk-away scenario if uninsured.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, states what changed and why, cites the preferred limits and offers the fallback (E&O 1M / cyber 2M) as instructed; deterministic checks confirm the insurance obligation is present and the operation applies.
Edit is additive only and does not disturb existing text, and it benefits the customer without duplicating another rule's commercial term.
